When the definition is identical, the two releases are compared with the same category classification, trimmed-text matching, order-insensitive pairing and duplicate-count rules as `diff` — a change in the order of entries alone never resets an item — scoped to the categories the **new template item** declares: an item declaring no `categories` compares all three categories, and a multi-category item compares every category it declares, categories absent from the target release included. Only when every compared category is completely unchanged (nothing added and nothing removed in that category) between the two releases is the old status kept and the id listed in `retained`; otherwise the item takes the new definition with `pending` status and the id is listed in `reset`. For example, when only the Added entries change a Fixed-scoped done item stays `done`, while losing one of two duplicate Fixed entries resets even the Fixed item. Old items that do not appear in the filtered target selection — whether filtered out because the target release no longer has any of their declared categories or missing from the new template — are removed, their ids following the old checklist order.

The result holds only `baseVersion`, `version`, `items`, `retained`, `reset`, `added` and `removed`, where `version` is the target version; `items` follows the target template order and each entry carries only the normalized `id`, `text`, `required` and `status`, so the result can be passed straight to `checklist`/`check` or `audit_checklist` against the target version. `retained`, `reset` and `added` hold ids in target template order, `removed` holds ids in old checklist order, and all four arrays are present even when empty. Template-declared status is ignored and status is never inferred from change texts. An invalid or unknown version (base or target), invalid store, checklist or template content, a checklist version mismatch, an empty filtered selection or a selection without any required item raises `ValueError`, and read failures raise `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects non-UTF-8 files, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in either file, printing a single-line `error` object with exit 2 for any of these and the single-line result with exit 0 on success. A missing store is treated as empty and then reports both versions as unknown. Neither success nor failure modifies the passed payloads, the input files or the store, or creates any file or directory, and mutating nested values in the returned result never reaches the passed inputs. The existing same-version rule of `reconcile_checklist` is unchanged.

`ReleaseDesk.update_checklist(version, updates, checklist_path)` applies a batch of status updates to a local checklist file, confirming each entry against the status currently stored, and `python3 release_desk.py update-checklist 1.2.0 updates.json checklist.json` reads the batch from a UTF-8 JSON file using the same `--store` selection and treats the third positional path as the write target. The version follows the existing version rules and must be registered (the whole store is validated first; a missing store is treated as empty and then reports the version as unknown), and the target checklist follows the existing checklist rules, including the rule that its declared version must equal the queried version and its at-least-one-required-item rule.

The updates value is an array, which may be empty; every entry holds exactly `id`, `expected` and `status` — a non-dict entry, a missing or extra field, or a structural root that is not an array is rejected. Ids follow the single-line checklist id rule (a trimmed, non-empty string with no carriage returns or newlines in the raw value), match case-sensitively after trimming surrounding whitespace with no Unicode normalization, and must be unique within the batch after normalization. `expected` and `status` must each be one of `done`, `pending` and `blocked`, and any status may switch to any other; a value that is already the target status is still checked. Every `expected` status is compared with the status read from the checklist, including entries whose target status would not change anything, and a single mismatch — or an id absent from the checklist — rejects the whole batch with `ValueError` before anything is written.

The result holds only `version`, `changed`, `items`, `updated` and `ready`. `items` keeps the checklist order and the normalized four fields, changing only the statuses of matched items; `updated` is always an array and lists, in checklist order, only the ids whose status actually changed; `ready` follows the existing readiness rule of every required item being `done`. `changed` is true only when at least one status actually changes. When it is true the target is replaced wholesale with a UTF-8 JSON object holding only `version` and `items`, ending in a newline; when it is false the target's bytes and modification time are left completely untouched. An empty batch is a valid run that still validates the version, the store and the whole checklist, changing nothing.

The target file must already exist and must not be a symbolic link, and it must not be the same file as the store or, on the CLI, as the updates file — textual path aliases and hard links are recognized — with violations raising `ValueError`; a missing target and any read or write failure raise `OSError`, and neither a missing target nor missing directories are ever created. An invalid version, an unknown release, an invalid checklist or store, an illegal update structure or id, a duplicate or unknown update id, an expected-status mismatch, non-UTF-8 bytes, a JSON syntax error or a repeated object key at any level raises `ValueError`. Any failure preserves the target's original bytes and never creates a file or directory, and success or failure never modifies the updates array, the updates file or the store. The CLI prints the single-line result with exit 0 on success and a single-line `error` object with exit 2 on failure.

`ReleaseDesk.preview_update_checklist(version, updates, checklist_path)` is a read-only dry run of the same batch: it confirms whether the whole batch would be accepted and shows the planned checklist and readiness without writing, and `python3 release_desk.py update-checklist 1.2.0 updates.json checklist.json --dry-run` runs it with the same positional arguments and `--store` selection; omitting the flag keeps the original writing behavior exactly. The preview follows the same public version, store, checklist, update-entry and id-matching rules as `update_checklist`, in the same order — the version must be registered after the whole store is validated (a missing store is treated as empty and then reports the version as unknown), the target must already exist, must not be a symbolic link and must not alias the store or, on the CLI, the updates file (textual aliases and hard links recognized), and non-UTF-8 bytes, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level are rejected. An empty updates array is a valid preview that still validates the whole store and the whole checklist. Illegal input, an unregistered version, a checklist version mismatch, an invalid store, non-UTF-8 bytes, a JSON syntax error or a repeated key raises `ValueError`; a read failure or a missing target raises `OSError`; neither success nor failure modifies the passed array, the updates file, the checklist file, its modification time or the store, and no file or directory is created.

Instead of raising, unknown ids and expected-status mismatches become conflict entries reported in updates-array order: each conflict holds only the normalized `id`, the `expected` status, `actual`, the target `status` and `reason`; `actual` is `null` with reason `unknown-id` for an id absent from the checklist, and `reason` is `status-mismatch` with the read status as `actual` otherwise. A target status that is already satisfied still has its `expected` status checked. The result holds only `version`, `canUpdate`, `changed`, `items`, `updated`, `ready` and `conflicts`, and every array is always present. With no conflicts `canUpdate` is true, `items` keeps the checklist order and normalized four fields changing only matched statuses, `updated` lists, in checklist order, only the ids whose status would actually change, and `changed` is true only when that array is non-empty; `ready` follows the existing rule that every required item is `done`. With any conflict `canUpdate` is false, `items` is the normalized original checklist unchanged, `updated` is empty, `changed` is false and no partial update is reported; `ready` then reflects the original checklist. A valid preview prints the single-line result with exit 0 even when it reports conflicts; any exception prints only a single-line `error` object with exit 2. Other public entry points keep their existing behavior.

`ReleaseDesk.preview_merge_checklist(version, base, incoming, current)` is a read-only three-way merge preview of same-version checklists, and `python3 release_desk.py merge-checklist 1.2.0 base.json incoming.json current.json` reads the common base, the incoming checklist and the current checklist from three UTF-8 JSON files in that order using the same `--store` selection. All three inputs follow the existing checklist rules — including the rule that each declared version must equal the queried version — the whole store is validated before the version is looked up (a missing store is treated as empty and then reports the version as unknown), and the version must be registered. Items are matched by their normalized ids, case-sensitively after trimming with no Unicode normalization, and compared as whole normalized items: only `id`, `text`, `required` and `status` take part, extra fields are ignored, and a missing item differs from any present one.

For each id, an incoming side equal to the base or to the current side keeps the current side; otherwise a current side equal to the base adopts the incoming side; every remaining case is one whole-item conflict that keeps the current side's presence state and content. Additions, deletions and modifications all follow this rule, non-conflicting changes still enter the preview, and item fields are never merged separately. The result holds only `version`, `canMerge`, `ready`, `items` and `conflicts`: `canMerge` is true only when no conflict was reported, and `ready` follows the existing rule that every required item is `done`. `items` carries only the four normalized fields, keeps the current-side item order and then appends, in incoming-side order, the preview items the current side lacks. `conflicts` is always an array, sorted by id in Unicode code point order, each entry holding only `id`, `base`, `incoming` and `current`, the last three being the complete normalized item or `null` when that side lacks the id. A preview that would be empty or would hold no required item raises `ValueError`, and this result validation applies to conflicting previews too.

An invalid or unregistered version, a declared-version mismatch, an invalid checklist or store, an empty preview or a preview without any required item raises `ValueError`, while a missing or unreadable file raises `OSError`; the CLI additionally rejects non-UTF-8 files, JSON syntax errors and repeated object keys at any level in any of the three files, printing only a single-line `error` object with exit 2. A valid preview — conflicts included — prints the single-line result with exit 0. Neither success nor failure modifies the passed payloads, the input files or the store, no file or directory is created, and mutating the returned data never reaches the inputs. Other public entry points keep their existing behavior.

`ReleaseDesk.resolve_merge_checklist(version, base, incoming, current, decisions)` is a read-only confirmation layer over `preview_merge_checklist`, and `python3 release_desk.py resolve-merge-checklist 1.2.0 base.json incoming.json current.json decisions.json` reads the three checklists and the decisions from four UTF-8 JSON files in that order using the same `--store` selection. `decisions` is a JSON object, possibly empty, mapping original preview conflict ids to either the string `"incoming"` or the string `"current"`; partial selections are allowed. Keys match the normalized conflict ids exactly — case-sensitively, without trimming surrounding whitespace or Unicode normalization — and a key that is not an original conflict id is rejected, as is any non-object decision value, non-string key or choice other than the two strings. Choosing a side adopts that side's complete item; item fields are never merged separately. When the chosen side lacks the id the item is deleted, and choosing a side whose content is unchanged still counts as a confirmed decision. Unchosen conflicts keep their original details (including the current side's presence state and content) and keep the current item in the checklist; their fields are never merged field by field.

The result holds only `version`, `canMerge`, `ready`, `items`, `conflicts` and `resolved`. `items` carries only the four normalized fields, follows the current-side item order and then appends, in incoming-side order, items the current side originally lacked; confirmed deletions are absent. `canMerge` is true only when `conflicts` is empty, and `ready` follows the existing rule that every required item is `done`. `conflicts` holds only the unconfirmed conflicts in the preview structure, and each `resolved` entry holds only `id` and the original `choice` string. A valid run prints the single-line result with exit 0 even when conflicts remain. Neither success nor failure modifies the passed objects, the input files or the store, no file or directory is created, and mutating the returned data never reaches the inputs. All other public entry points keep their existing behavior.

`ReleaseDesk.apply_merge_checklist(version, base, incoming, expected, decisions, current_path)` saves a confirmed merge to a local checklist file, and `python3 release_desk.py apply-merge-checklist 1.2.0 base.json incoming.json expected.json decisions.json current.json` reads the base, incoming and expected checklists plus the decisions from four UTF-8 JSON files in that order using the same `--store` selection and treats the fifth path as the write target. The version, checklist, decisions, store and version-registration checks follow `resolve-merge-checklist` exactly, with the expected checklist validated like every other checklist. The target file must already exist and must not be a symbolic link, and it must not be the same file as the store or as any of the four input files — textual path aliases and hard links are recognized — with violations raising `ValueError`; a missing target or any read or write failure raises `OSError`, and neither a missing target nor missing directories are ever created. The result holds only `version`, `changed`, `items`, `resolved` and `ready`, where `items` and `resolved` carry the same content and ordering as the corresponding `resolve_merge_checklist` result. `changed` is true only when the normalized item sequence differs from the read one; then the target is replaced wholesale with UTF-8 JSON holding only `version` and `items` and ending in a newline, and when it is false the target's bytes and modification time are left untouched. 34	def _validate_json_value(value, seen=None, *, require_object=False):

113	def _json_values_equal(base, target):
114	    # Recursive JSON equality: object key order is ignored, array order counts.
115	    if isinstance(base, bool) or isinstance(target, bool):
116	        return type(base) is bool and type(target) is bool and base == target
117	    if base is None or target is None:
118	        return base is None and target is None
119	    if isinstance(base, (int, float)) and isinstance(target, (int, float)):
120	        # Numerically equal integers and floats compare equal.
121	        return base == target
122	    if isinstance(base, str) or isinstance(target, str):
123	        return isinstance(base, str) and isinstance(target, str) and base == target
124	    if isinstance(base, dict) or isinstance(target, dict):
125	        if not (isinstance(base, dict) and isinstance(target, dict)):
126	            return False
127	        if base.keys() != target.keys():
128	            return False

132	            return False

134	            _json_values_equal(base[index], target[index]) for index in range(len(base)))

276	def _atomic_write(path, content):
277	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

279	    try:

444	    def check_dependencies(self, version, checklist, dependencies):
445	        # Read-only dependency-aware readiness check over a declared checklist:
446	        # declared statuses are kept and a blocked effective status is layered
447	        # on top from direct prerequisites that are not themselves effectively
448	        # done. Nothing is written and the passed objects are never mutated.
449	        if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
450	            raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
451	        items = self._validated_checklist(checklist, version)
452	        prerequisites = self._validated_dependencies(dependencies, {item["id"] for item in items})
453	        # The whole store is validated before the version is looked up; a
454	        # missing store is treated as empty and then reports it as unknown.
455	        records = self._read_store()
456	        if version not in records:
457	            raise ValueError("unknown release")
458	        status_by_id = {item["id"]: item["status"] for item in items}
459	        effective = {}
460	
461	        def effective_status(item_id):
462	            # Memoized effective status over the validated acyclic graph. A
463	            # declaration counts only when every direct prerequisite is
464	            # effectively done; otherwise the item is blocked no matter what
465	            # it declared, so blocking propagates layer by layer without
466	            # listing transitive prerequisites.
467	            if item_id not in effective:
468	                status = status_by_id[item_id]
469	                if any(effective_status(prerequisite) != "done"
470	                       for prerequisite in prerequisites.get(item_id, ())):
471	                    status = "blocked"
472	                effective[item_id] = status
473	            return effective[item_id]
474	
475	        result_items, ready = [], True
476	        for item in items:
477	            item_id = item["id"]
478	            effect = effective_status(item_id)
479	            waiting = [prerequisite for prerequisite in prerequisites.get(item_id, ())
480	                       if effective_status(prerequisite) != "done"]
481	            result_items.append({"id": item["id"], "text": item["text"],
482	                                 "required": item["required"], "status": item["status"],
483	                                 "effectiveStatus": effect, "waiting": waiting})
484	            # Optional items never decide readiness themselves, but an
485	            # effectively blocked prerequisite keeps a required item blocked.
486	            if item["required"] and effect != "done":
487	                ready = False
488	        return {"version": version, "ready": ready, "items": result_items}

490	    @staticmethod
491	    def _validated_dependencies(dependencies, known_ids):
492	        # Validate the dependency map: an object mapping normalized item ids
493	        # to arrays of normalized prerequisite ids, each following the
494	        # checklist single-line id rule. Keys, array entries, unknown ends,
495	        # self dependencies and cycles are all rejected; empty maps and empty
496	        # arrays mean "no prerequisites".
497	        if not isinstance(dependencies, dict):
498	            raise ValueError("dependencies must be a JSON object")
499	        normalized = {}
500	        seen_keys = set()
501	        for item_id, prerequisites in dependencies.items():
502	            if not isinstance(item_id, str) or not item_id.strip() or "\n" in item_id or "\r" in item_id:
503	                raise ValueError("dependency item id must be a non-empty single-line string")
504	            item_id = item_id.strip()
505	            # Case-sensitive, no trimming beyond the ends, no Unicode normalization.
506	            if item_id in seen_keys:
507	                raise ValueError("dependency item id must be unique")
508	            seen_keys.add(item_id)
509	            if not isinstance(prerequisites, list):
510	                raise ValueError("dependency prerequisites must be arrays of item ids")
511	            ordered, seen = [], set()
512	            for prerequisite in prerequisites:
513	                if (not isinstance(prerequisite, str) or not prerequisite.strip()
514	                        or "\n" in prerequisite or "\r" in prerequisite):
515	                    raise ValueError("dependency item id must be a non-empty single-line string")
516	                prerequisite = prerequisite.strip()
517	                # Case-sensitive, no trimming beyond the ends, no Unicode normalization.
518	                if prerequisite in seen:
519	                    raise ValueError("dependency prerequisite ids must be unique within one item")
520	                seen.add(prerequisite)
521	                ordered.append(prerequisite)
522	            normalized[item_id] = ordered
523	        for item_id, prerequisites in normalized.items():
524	            if item_id not in known_ids:
525	                raise ValueError("dependency item id must exist in the checklist")
526	            for prerequisite in prerequisites:
527	                if prerequisite not in known_ids:
528	                    raise ValueError("dependency prerequisite id must exist in the checklist")
529	                if prerequisite == item_id:
530	                    raise ValueError("dependencies must not contain a self dependency")
531	        # Reject every remaining cycle, including cycles over optional items:
532	        # resolve every id with an empty trail set.
533	        visiting = set()
534	        settled = set()
535	
536	        def visit(node):
537	            if node in settled:
538	                return
539	            if node in visiting:
540	                raise ValueError("dependencies must not contain a cycle")
541	            visiting.add(node)
542	            for prerequisite in normalized.get(node, ()):
543	                visit(prerequisite)
544	            visiting.remove(node)
545	            settled.add(node)
546	
547	        for item_id in normalized:
548	            visit(item_id)
549	        return normalized

634	    def release_record_with_dependencies(self, version, checklist, template,
635	                                         rollback, dependencies):

637	        # map: the audit follows audit_checklist and the dependency report

639	        # when both reports are ready. An unfinished optional item never
640	        # blocks the record by itself, but as a direct or indirect
641	        # prerequisite of a required item it blocks through the existing
642	        # effective-status propagation. The returned snapshot is detached
643	        # from every passed object and carries no generated timestamp, so
644	        # identical inputs yield identical records.

654	        # undeclared item freezes to an empty array and declared
655	        # prerequisites keep their dependency-array order.

659	                "changes": copy.deepcopy(changes),
660	                "notes": self.notes(version),
661	                "audit": copy.deepcopy(audit),
662	                "rollback": {"targetVersion": target_version, "steps": steps},
663	                "dependencies": frozen,
664	                "dependencyCheck": copy.deepcopy(dependency_check)}

666	    def _validated_rollback(self, rollback, release_version):
667	        # Validate the rollback plan: a strict {"targetVersion", "steps"}
668	        # object. targetVersion is null or a registered version numerically
669	        # smaller than the release; steps is a non-empty array of single-line
670	        # strings, stored trimmed with order and duplicates preserved.
671	        if not isinstance(rollback, dict):
672	            raise ValueError("rollback plan must be a JSON object")
673	        if set(rollback) != {"targetVersion", "steps"}:
674	            raise ValueError("rollback plan requires exactly targetVersion and steps")
675	        target_version = rollback["targetVersion"]
676	        if target_version is not None:
677	            if not isinstance(target_version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, target_version):
678	                raise ValueError("rollback targetVersion must be null or a valid version")
679	            records = self._read_store()
680	            if target_version not in records:
681	                raise ValueError("rollback targetVersion must be a registered release")
682	            if _version_order(target_version) >= _version_order(release_version):
683	                raise ValueError("rollback targetVersion must be smaller than the release version")
684	        steps = rollback["steps"]
685	        if not isinstance(steps, list) or not steps:
686	            raise ValueError("rollback steps must be a non-empty array of strings")
687	        normalized = []
688	        for step in steps:
689	            if not isinstance(step, str) or "\n" in step or "\r" in step or not step.strip():
690	                raise ValueError("rollback steps must be non-empty single-line strings")
691	            normalized.append(step.strip())
692	        return target_version, normalized

694	    def reconcile_checklist(self, version, checklist, template):
695	        # Read-only update of a same-version checklist against a revised
696	        # template: unchanged definitions keep their status, redefined items
697	        # reset to pending, new items are added and inapplicable items drop.
698	        if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
699	            raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
700	        items = self._validated_checklist(checklist, version)
701	        template_items = self._validated_template(template)
702	        # The whole store is validated before the version is looked up.
703	        records = self._read_store()
704	        if version not in records:
705	            raise ValueError("unknown release")
706	        selected = self._applicable_template_items(template_items, records[version])
707	        # Ids match case-sensitively after trimming, without Unicode normalization.
708	        previous = {item["id"]: item for item in items}
709	        reconciled, retained, reset, added = [], [], [], []
710	        for expected in selected:
711	            item_id = expected["id"]
712	            actual = previous.get(item_id)
713	            if actual is None:
714	                reconciled.append(dict(expected))
715	                added.append(item_id)
716	            elif actual["text"] != expected["text"] or actual["required"] != expected["required"]:
717	                # A redefined item takes the new definition and returns to pending.
718	                reconciled.append(dict(expected))
719	                reset.append(item_id)
720	            else:
721	                reconciled.append({"id": item_id, "text": expected["text"],
722	                                   "required": expected["required"], "status": actual["status"]})
723	                retained.append(item_id)
724	        selected_ids = {item["id"] for item in selected}
725	        removed = [item["id"] for item in items if item["id"] not in selected_ids]
726	        return {"version": version, "items": reconciled,
727	                "retained": retained, "reset": reset, "added": added, "removed": removed}

729	    def migrate_checklist(self, base_version, target_version, checklist, template):
730	        # Read-only cross-version migration: only progress still backed by the
731	        # target release is inherited. Unlike reconcile_checklist, a same-id
732	        # item whose definition is unchanged keeps its status solely when the
733	        # change entries covered by the item's template categories are
734	        # identical between the two registered releases.
735	        for version in (base_version, target_version):
736	            if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
737	                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
738	        # The checklist is validated against the base version it declares; the
739	        # template is validated in full before the target filter is applied.
740	        items = self._validated_checklist(checklist, base_version)
741	        template_items = self._validated_template(template)
742	        # The whole store is validated before either version is looked up.
743	        records = self._read_store()
744	        if base_version not in records:
745	            raise ValueError("unknown release")
746	        if target_version not in records:
747	            raise ValueError("unknown release")
748	        selected = self._applicable_template_items(template_items, records[target_version])
749	        # Reuse the diff classification as the change comparison; the scope
750	        # filters it down to the categories a template item declares. When the
751	        # item declares none every category is compared, categories not present
752	        # in the target release included.
753	        added, removed, unchanged = self._diff_entries(
754	            self._clean_changes(records[base_version]),
755	            self._clean_changes(records[target_version]))
756	        changed_by_category = {}
757	        for category in CATEGORIES:
758	            changed_by_category[category] = any(
759	                entry["category"] == category for entry in added + removed)
760	        previous = {item["id"]: item for item in items}
761	        definitions = {item["id"]: item for item in template_items}
762	        migrated, retained, reset, added_ids = [], [], [], []
763	        for expected in selected:
764	            item_id = expected["id"]
765	            actual = previous.get(item_id)
766	            if actual is None:
767	                migrated.append(dict(expected))
768	                added_ids.append(item_id)
769	            elif actual["text"] != expected["text"] or actual["required"] != expected["required"]:
770	                migrated.append(dict(expected))
771	                reset.append(item_id)
772	            else:
773	                categories = definitions[item_id]["categories"]
774	                scope = CATEGORIES if categories is None else tuple(categories)
775	                if all(not changed_by_category[category] for category in scope):
776	                    migrated.append({"id": item_id, "text": expected["text"],
777	                                     "required": expected["required"], "status": actual["status"]})
778	                    retained.append(item_id)
779	                else:
780	                    migrated.append(dict(expected))
781	                    reset.append(item_id)
782	        selected_ids = {item["id"] for item in selected}
783	        removed_ids = [item["id"] for item in items if item["id"] not in selected_ids]
784	        return {"baseVersion": base_version, "version": target_version,
785	                "items": migrated,
786	                "retained": retained, "reset": reset, "added": added_ids,
787	                "removed": removed_ids}

789	    def update_checklist(self, version, updates, checklist_path):
790	        # Batch-update the statuses of a local checklist file after confirming
791	        # every expected status still matches the read bytes: one mismatch
792	        # rejects the whole batch. Only when at least one status changes is the
793	        # target replaced wholesale with UTF-8 JSON ending in a newline;

800	        # whose target status would not change anything.
801	        for item_id, expected, _status in normalized_updates:
802	            actual = status_by_id.get(item_id)
803	            if actual is None:
804	                raise ValueError("update item id must exist in the checklist")
805	            if actual != expected:
806	                raise ValueError("update expected status does not match the checklist")

813	        ready = all(item["status"] == "done" for item in resulting if item["required"])
814	        return {"version": version, "changed": changed, "items": resulting,
815	                "updated": updated, "ready": ready}

821	        # order instead of raised, and nothing is ever written.

826	        # status is already satisfied; conflicts keep the updates-array order.

830	            if actual is None:

841	            updated = []
842	            changed = False
843	        else:
844	            can_update = True

846	            changed = bool(updated)
847	        ready = all(item["status"] == "done" for item in resulting if item["required"])

872	    def resolve_merge_checklist(self, version, base, incoming, current, decisions):
873	        # Read-only confirmation layer over preview_merge_checklist: decisions
874	        # maps original preview conflict ids to "incoming" or "current"; empty
875	        # and partial maps are allowed. A chosen side is adopted as one whole
876	        # item and choosing a side that lacks the id deletes the item.
877	        # Unchosen conflicts keep their original details and the current side.
878	        if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
879	            raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
880	        base_items = self._validated_checklist(base, version)
881	        incoming_items = self._validated_checklist(incoming, version)
882	        current_items = self._validated_checklist(current, version)
883	        choices = _validated_merge_choices(decisions)
884	        # The whole store is validated before the version is looked up; a
885	        # missing store is treated as empty and then reports it as unknown.
886	        records = self._read_store()
887	        if version not in records:
888	            raise ValueError("unknown release")
889	        merged, conflicts = self._merge_classification(
890	            base_items, incoming_items, current_items)
891	        # The original preview must itself stay a legal checklist before any
892	        # decision is applied.
893	        self._validate_merge_items(
894	            self._ordered_merge_items(merged, incoming_items, current_items))
895	        conflict_ids = {entry["id"] for entry in conflicts}
896	        # Keys match the normalized conflict ids exactly: case-sensitive, with
897	        # no trimming or Unicode normalization, and never at a non-conflict id.
898	        for item_id in choices:

    def diff(self, base_version, target_version):
        for version in (base_version, target_version):
            if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
        records = self._read_store()
        base = self._checked_entries(records, base_version)
        target = self._checked_entries(records, target_version)
        added, removed, unchanged = self._diff_entries(base, target)
        return {"baseVersion": base_version, "targetVersion": target_version,
                "added": added, "removed": removed, "unchanged": unchanged}

    @staticmethod
    def _diff_entries(base, target):
        # Classify cleaned entries of target relative to base, per category in
        # fixed order; duplicates pair up by occurrence within each category.
        added, removed, unchanged = [], [], []
        for category in CATEGORIES:
            base_entries = [entry for entry in base if entry["category"] == category]
            target_entries = [entry for entry in target if entry["category"] == category]
            available = Counter(entry["text"] for entry in base_entries)
            for entry in target_entries:
                if available[entry["text"]] > 0:
                    available[entry["text"]] -= 1
                    unchanged.append(entry)
                else:
                    added.append(entry)
            matched = Counter(entry["text"] for entry in target_entries)
            for entry in base_entries:
                if matched[entry["text"]] > 0:
                    matched[entry["text"]] -= 1
                else:
                    removed.append(entry)
        return added, removed, unchanged

    @staticmethod
    def _checked_entries(records, version):
        if version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        return ReleaseDesk._clean_changes(records[version])

    def diff_config(self, base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config):
        # Read-only structural comparison of two externally supplied
        # configurations for two registered versions. Nothing is stored and
        # the configurations are never inferred from change entries.
        for version in (base_version, target_version):
            if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
        _validated_config(base_config)
        _validated_config(target_config)
        # The whole store is validated before either version is looked up.
        records = self._read_store()
        if base_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        if target_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        added, removed, changed = [], [], []
        _diff_config_values(base_config, target_config, "", added, removed, changed)
        # Paths sort by Unicode code point, not by locale.
        added.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["path"])
        removed.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["path"])
        changed.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["path"])
        return {"baseVersion": base_version, "targetVersion": target_version,
                "added": added, "removed": removed, "changed": changed}

    def preview_config(self, base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config, current_config):
        # Read-only three-way preview of applying the base->target plan onto
        # the current configuration. Nothing is stored and the configurations
        # are never inferred from change entries.
        for version in (base_version, target_version):
            if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
        _validated_config(base_config)
        _validated_config(target_config)
        _validated_config(current_config)
        # The whole store is validated before either version is looked up.
        records = self._read_store()
        if base_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        if target_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        conflicts = []
        preview = _preview_config_values(base_config, target_config, current_config, "", conflicts)
        # Paths sort by Unicode code point, not by locale.
        conflicts.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["path"])
        return {"baseVersion": base_version, "targetVersion": target_version,
                "canApply": not conflicts, "config": preview, "conflicts": conflicts}

    def resolve_config(self, base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config,
                       current_config, decisions):
        # Read-only three-way resolution with per-path conflict choices. The
        # decisions map original preview_config conflict paths verbatim to
        # "target", "current" or a custom {"present", "value"?} decision;
        # nothing is stored or inferred from entries.
        for version in (base_version, target_version):
            if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
        _validated_config(base_config)
        _validated_config(target_config)
        _validated_config(current_config)
        choices = _validated_decisions(decisions)
        # The whole store is validated before either version is looked up.
        records = self._read_store()
        if base_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        if target_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        conflicts = []
        _preview_config_values(base_config, target_config, current_config, "", conflicts)
        conflict_paths = {entry["path"] for entry in conflicts}
        # Keys match the original conflict paths verbatim, using the same JSON
        # Pointer escaping: no trimming, normalization or subpath selection.
        for path in choices:
            if path not in conflict_paths:
                raise ValueError("decision path is not a conflict path")
        resolved = []
        config = _resolve_config_values(
            base_config, target_config, current_config, "", choices, resolved)
        chosen_paths = {entry["path"] for entry in resolved}
        remaining = [entry for entry in conflicts if entry["path"] not in chosen_paths]
        # Paths sort by Unicode code point, not by locale.
        remaining.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["path"])
        resolved.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["path"])
        return {"baseVersion": base_version, "targetVersion": target_version,
                "canApply": not remaining, "config": config,
                "conflicts": remaining, "resolved": resolved}

    def apply_config(self, base_version, target_version, base_config, target_config,
                     expected_config, decisions, current_path):
        # Applying a confirmed plan to a local configuration file: the file is
        # read, checked against the expected snapshot, resolved exactly like
        # resolve_config and, only when the result differs, replaced wholesale
        # with UTF-8 JSON ending in a newline. Nothing else is modified.
        for version in (base_version, target_version):
            if not isinstance(version, str) or not re.fullmatch(VERSION_PATTERN, version):
                raise ValueError("version must have three nonnegative numeric components")
        _validated_config(base_config)
        _validated_config(target_config)
        _validated_config(expected_config)
        choices = _validated_decisions(decisions)
        # The whole store is validated before either version is looked up.
        records = self._read_store()
        if base_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        if target_version not in records:
            raise ValueError("unknown release")
        path = Path(current_path)
        if path.is_symlink():
            raise ValueError("current configuration file must not be a symbolic link")
        if _same_file(self.path, path):
            raise ValueError("current configuration file must not be the same file as the store")
        # A missing target or an unreadable file raises OSError unchanged.
        try:
            raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
            raise ValueError("current configuration file must contain UTF-8 encoded JSON") from exc
        try:
            current_config = _loads_unique(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise ValueError("current configuration file must contain UTF-8 encoded JSON") from exc
        _validated_config(current_config)
        if not _json_values_equal(expected_config, current_config):
            raise ValueError("current configuration does not match the expected configuration")
        conflicts = []
        _preview_config_values(base_config, target_config, current_config, "", conflicts)
        conflict_paths = {entry["path"] for entry in conflicts}
        for decision_path in choices:
            if decision_path not in conflict_paths:
                raise ValueError("decision path is not a conflict path")
        resolved = []
        config = _resolve_config_values(
            base_config, target_config, current_config, "", choices, resolved)
        chosen_paths = {entry["path"] for entry in resolved}
        if any(entry["path"] not in chosen_paths for entry in conflicts):
            raise ValueError("unresolved conflicts remain")
        # Paths sort by Unicode code point, not by locale.
        resolved.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["path"])
        changed = not _json_values_equal(config, current_config)
        if changed:
            content = json.dumps(config, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
            _atomic_write(path, content)
        return {"baseVersion": base_version, "targetVersion": target_version,
                "changed": changed, "config": config, "resolved": resolved}

class CheckDependenciesTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT)
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.path = Path(self.temp.name) / "releases.json"
        self.desk = ReleaseDesk(self.path)
        self.desk.add("1.2.0", [{"category": "Added", "text": "One"}])

    def payload(self, *items):
        if not items:
            items = (
                {"id": "a", "text": "A", "required": True, "status": "done"},
                {"id": "b", "text": "B", "required": True, "status": "done"},
                {"id": "c", "text": "C", "required": False, "status": "pending"},
            )
        return {"version": "1.2.0", "items": list(items)}

    def test_no_dependencies_matches_check(self):
        for dependencies in ({}, {"a": [], "b": [], "c": []}):
            report = self.desk.check_dependencies("1.2.0", self.payload(), dependencies)
            self.assertEqual(set(report), {"version", "ready", "items"})
            self.assertTrue(report["ready"])
            self.assertEqual([item["id"] for item in report["items"]], ["a", "b", "c"])
            for item in report["items"]:
                self.assertEqual(set(item),
                                 {"id", "text", "required", "status", "effectiveStatus", "waiting"})
                self.assertEqual(item["effectiveStatus"], item["status"])
                self.assertEqual(item["waiting"], [])

    def test_chain_blocks_layer_by_layer_with_direct_only_waiting(self):
        # The spec example: A depends on B, B on C; A and B declare done while
        # C is pending. Both are blocked effectively, and A waits only on B.
        payload = self.payload()
        report = self.desk.check_dependencies("1.2.0", payload, {"a": ["b"], "b": ["c"]})
        effects = {item["id"]: item for item in report["items"]}
        self.assertFalse(report["ready"])
        self.assertEqual(effects["a"]["status"], "done")
        self.assertEqual(effects["a"]["effectiveStatus"], "blocked")
        self.assertEqual(effects["a"]["waiting"], ["b"])
        self.assertEqual(effects["b"]["effectiveStatus"], "blocked")
        self.assertEqual(effects["b"]["waiting"], ["c"])
        self.assertEqual(effects["c"]["effectiveStatus"], "pending")
        self.assertEqual(effects["c"]["waiting"], [])

    def test_undone_prerequisite_blocks_any_declared_status(self):
        payload = self.payload(
            {"id": "a", "text": "A", "required": True, "status": "pending"},
            {"id": "b", "text": "B", "required": True, "status": "blocked"},
            {"id": "c", "text": "C", "required": False, "status": "pending"},
        )
        report = self.desk.check_dependencies("1.2.0", payload, {"a": ["c"], "b": ["c"]})
        effects = {item["id"]: item["effectiveStatus"] for item in report["items"]}
        self.assertEqual(effects, {"a": "blocked", "b": "blocked", "c": "pending"})

    def test_waiting_lists_only_not_done_direct_prerequisites_in_array_order(self):
        payload = self.payload(
            {"id": "a", "text": "A", "required": True, "status": "done"},
            {"id": "b", "text": "B", "required": False, "status": "done"},
            {"id": "c", "text": "C", "required": False, "status": "pending"},
            {"id": "d", "text": "D", "required": False, "status": "blocked"},
        )
        deps = {"a": ["b", "c", "d"]}
        report = self.desk.check_dependencies("1.2.0", payload, deps)
        item_a = report["items"][0]
        # b is effectively done and drops out; waiting keeps only the not-done
        # direct prerequisites in dependency-array order, never transitive ones.
        self.assertEqual(item_a["waiting"], ["c", "d"])
        self.assertEqual(item_a["effectiveStatus"], "blocked")

    def test_optional_items_and_readiness(self):
        # A blocked optional item never decides readiness on its own...
        optional_blocked = self.payload(
            {"id": "a", "text": "A", "required": True, "status": "done"},

        return {"version": "1.2.0", "items": list(items)}

    def test_spec_example_chain_reports_only_leaf_reason(self):
        # A (required, done) depends on B (optional, done), B on pending C:
        # only C is a reason, with A affected through the path A, B, C.
        payload = self.payload(
            {"id": "a", "text": "A", "required": True, "status": "done"},
            {"id": "b", "text": "B", "required": False, "status": "done"},
            {"id": "c", "text": "C", "required": False, "status": "pending"},
        )
        report = self.desk.explain_dependencies("1.2.0", payload, {"a": ["b"], "b": ["c"]})
        self.assertEqual(set(report), {"version", "ready", "reasons"})
        self.assertEqual(report["version"], "1.2.0")
        self.assertFalse(report["ready"])
        self.assertEqual(report["reasons"], [
            {"id": "c", "text": "C", "required": False, "status": "pending",
             "affected": [{"id": "a", "path": ["a", "b", "c"]}]}])

    def test_ready_report_has_empty_reasons(self):

            {"id": "a", "text": "A", "required": True, "status": "done"},
            {"id": "b", "text": "B", "required": False, "status": "pending"},
        )
        for dependencies in ({}, {"a": []}, {"b": []}):
            report = self.desk.explain_dependencies("1.2.0", payload, dependencies)
            self.assertTrue(report["ready"])

A missing store is treated as empty and then reports the version as unknown, and neither success nor failure modifies the store, the input files or the passed payloads, or creates any file or directory.
